title: Hostel water meter

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own hostel story, statement, tests, solutions and editorial; the prefix-sum idea is classic, the words and examples are ours.

statement:
The warden of Ganga Hostel reads the water meter every night and writes down how many litres the hostel used that day. After `n` days, the mess committee has `q` questions, each of the form: **how many litres did the hostel use from day `l` to day `r`, both days included?**

Answer every question. Days are numbered from 1. Every question has `l ≤ r`, so each answer is a sum of at least one day; a range of days that all read 0 has the answer 0.
input_format:
The first line has two integers `n` and `q`.

The second line has `n` integers `a_1 a_2 ... a_n`: the litres used on each day.

Each of the next `q` lines has two integers `l` and `r`: one question.
output_format: Print `q` lines. Line `k` is the total litres used from day `l` to day `r` of the `k`-th question. Totals can exceed 2^31 − 1, so use 64-bit integers.

statement_rules.output_when_empty: There is always at least one question and every range has at least one day; a range of zero readings prints 0.
statement_rules.multiple_answers: Each question has exactly one total.

solutions.why: Adds every range day by day: O(n) per question, O(n·q) = 1.5·10^9 steps on the largest test.
Keeps the prefix sums in 32-bit int, so a total above 2^31 − 1 wraps around.
Subtracts prefix[l] instead of prefix[l − 1], so day l itself is left out.

tests.explanation: Days 1–2 both read 0, so the total is 0 and is still printed. Days 1–3 add the 7 of day 3.

tests.note: zero answer and a non-zero one

hints: Count the work: one question can cover every day, and there are many questions. How many additions does adding each range directly cost in the worst case?
Many questions share days. Is there a running total you could compute once, so that a range becomes a difference of two running totals?
Let prefix[i] be the total of days 1..i, with prefix[0] = 0. Then days l..r total prefix[r] − prefix[l − 1]. Use 64-bit numbers.

approaches.name: brute
approaches.summary: For every question, add the readings from day l to day r. Correct, but up to 1.5·10^9 additions on the largest input.

approaches.name: better
approaches.summary: Store the total of each block of about √n days; a question adds whole blocks plus the loose days at its two ends.

approaches.name: optimal
approaches.summary: Build prefix sums once (prefix[0] = 0); each question is prefix[r] − prefix[l − 1] in 64-bit arithmetic.

visuals.alt: Building prefix sums for the readings 120, 80, 0, 200, 150, 90 one day at a time (0, 120, 200, 200, 400, 550, 640), then answering (1,3), (2,5) and (4,4) as 200 − 0, 550 − 120 and 400 − 200.

frames.note: prefix[0] = 0: the total of no days

revision_card.front: Many questions: the sum of a[l..r] (1-indexed) on a fixed array. Method, formula, and two traps?
revision_card.back: Prefix sums: prefix[0] = 0, prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + a[i-1]. Sum(l..r) = prefix[r] − prefix[l − 1]. O(n + q). Traps: subtracting prefix[l] (loses day l); 32-bit totals overflow.
